# Tier-2 Dependencies - Require Manual Review Before Merge
#
# Criteria (any match triggers tier-2):
# - New direct dependencies (not transitive)
# - Handles: network/IO, cryptography, unsafe code, financial data
# - Repo signals: <100 GitHub stars, unmaintained (>1yr), single maintainer
#
# Format:
#   crate           - tier-2, any version change needs review
#   crate=x.y.z     - PINNED, exact version required
#
# Pinned entries include: # review-date | risk-factors
# The auto-merge workflow reads this file and applies 'tier-2' label.

ibapi=3.2.0  # 2026-07-09 | Financial protocol, community-maintained, no official SDK. Reviewed 3.0.1->3.2.0: zero unsafe, no build.rs, dependency tree byte-identical vs 3.0.1 (only the version line differs), only opens a caller-supplied TWS socket + opt-in local recorder dir (IBAPI_RECORDING_DIR).
binance-sdk=52.0.0  # 2026-06-04 | Exchange SDK, signing/IO. PINNED: margin user-data stream couples to 3 `binance_sdk::common` internals (lower-stability than the public per-market API). ANY bump MUST re-verify all 3 before merge:
#   1. common::websocket::WebsocketApi::send_message      — signature + WebsocketMessageSendOptions signing fields (margin WS subscribe send)
#   2. ws.common.events.subscribe (WebsocketEventEmitter) — receive/event-callback path (margin WS event delivery)
#   3. common::utils::send_request                        — signature + HMAC signing + X-MBX-APIKEY header (hand-rolled `userListenToken` POST; SDK binds no endpoint for it)
# Background: legacy margin listen-key user-data API retired 2026-02-20; SDK binds only the dead endpoint, so the live `userListenToken` flow is hand-rolled atop these internals.
quick-xml  # 2026-07-08 | New direct dep (XML parsing of broker Flex statements). Reviewed @ 0.41.0: #![forbid(unsafe_code)] crate-wide, zero net-new transitive deps (serde+memchr only, both already in tree), no RUSTSEC advisories, de-facto-standard parser. Not pinned — any version bump still needs review.
parquet  # 2026-07-28 | New direct dep (Parquet decode of provider bulk exports). Reviewed @ 59.1.0, Apache-2.0, apache/arrow-rs (ASF-governed, ~65M downloads). MUST stay `default-features = false, features = ["zstd"]` — that is what keeps `arrow` out, and re-enabling defaults pulls arrow-array/buffer/data/schema/select/ipc, base64, brotli, flate2, lz4, snap and simdutf8 in one line. Under the pinned feature set: no build.rs; no network, process-spawn or env access anywhere in the library (the only `env::var` is in `src/bin/parquet-fromcsv.rs`, a CLI binary we do not build); 19 `unsafe` sites in the compiled paths, all in columnar decode hot spots (bit packing, RLE, byte-stream-split, bloom filter) and idiomatic for the crate class. Tree is 13 direct deps. Net-new surface, measured by diffing Cargo.lock before/after rather than eyeballed: COMPILED ON ORDINARY TARGETS — paste, seq-macro, twox-hash, libm, and a second major of ahash (0.8.12, now built alongside the pre-existing 0.7.8). libm is not a new dependency edge: it arrives because parquet's tree turns on the `libm` feature of the already-present num-traits. LOCKFILE-ONLY — const-random and const-random-macro enter Cargo.lock via ahash 0.8 but are target-gated and absent from `cargo tree` on every target we ship; they would build only on no-std-ish targets. Re-check them if this workspace ever targets one: const-random-macro is a build-time proc-macro pulling getrandom + tiny-keccak, i.e. a compile-time RNG. ALREADY PRESENT, not new — zstd/zstd-safe/zstd-sys, chrono, bytes, hashbrown, half, num-*, getrandom, once_cell, zerocopy, tiny-keccak. Verified the arrow-free row/record API compiles and decodes real 4-column and 7-column artifacts (370,531 rows) — the feature reduction is real, not theoretical. Known advisory: RUSTSEC-2024-0436 on the transitive `paste` — INFORMATIONAL "unmaintained", not a vulnerability; paste is a compile-time proc-macro with zero deps, zero unsafe, and a build.rs that only runs `rustc --version`. Accepted; it arrives via parquet so it is not ours to swap. Not pinned — any version bump still needs review, and must re-check that `arrow` has not become non-optional.
